attribution.note: Zitron restates his own repeated argument in his own newsletter and endorses it. He is not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: An unhedged 'will lead it to ruin' is a forecast. The 'current trajectory' qualifier is kept, and no deadline is added.

contract.note: Reading ruin as a severe, sustained, sector-wide loss is fair and ordinary. Because there is no deadline or magnitude, the result depends on the evaluator's reading. The contract rightly says growth alone cannot refute the claim.

evidence.note: Goldman, April 2026: tech stocks fell but sector earnings stayed strong. That shows weakness, not ruin, and cannot settle an open-ended forecast.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. No sector-wide collapse tied to the described trajectory is documented, so the early-resolution rule is not met. Strong earnings by April 2026 do not refute an open-ended forecast. The claim remains unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his own essay.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the 'less discerning' trend and the three examples he gives.

contract.note: 'Less discerning' plainly means standards got worse compared with before. Separating training data from retrieved search results is a fair, ordinary distinction.

evidence.note: Google's own account says AI Overviews draw on search results, not just training data. This undercuts the cited examples as proof about training data but does not refute the trend. It is a company disclosure.
Meta describes quality filtering for Llama 3. This is one company's self-description, not a comparative industry-wide measure.
Confirms Meta used synthetic data but says nothing about whether it was selected carelessly or whether standards declined.

reviews.rationale: No before-and-after audit or documented relaxation of training-data standards is in the packet. The examples Zitron cites appear to stem from search retrieval, and Meta's filtering is self-reported. Nothing establishes or refutes an industry-wide decline, so the claim is unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own characterization in his own essay.

semantics.note: The proposition captures his core assertions: the strategic bet, the integration, the disregard for usefulness and the investor motive. Dropping the 'decaying empires' aside is acceptable.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair. The June 2024 window and the reading of the motive are the evaluator's choices. The motive and 'little regard' parts need evidence beyond product launches.

evidence.note: Google's June 2024 Gemini-in-Gmail launch backs the integration part for Google only. It says nothing about utility or motive.
Meta's June 2024 rollout across its apps backs the integration part for Meta only. It says nothing about motive.
April 2024 interview, outside the window: a Google Cloud executive names customer value as a priority. This is self-description and only qualifies the disregard claim.

reviews.rationale: Integration is documented for Google and Meta but not for Microsoft. Nothing establishes that usefulness was disregarded, that investor signaling was the main motive, or that the companies' futures depended on generative AI. No element is refuted either. The claim as a whole is unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his own essay.

semantics.note: 'Any future improvements will be marginal' is an unhedged, universal forecast. The present-tense 'hitting a wall' is folded into it.

contract.note: Including reasoning and inference-compute systems fits his broad term 'generative AI'. 'Marginal' has no threshold, so the result depends on the evaluator's reading of it. The early-resolution rule is reasonable.

evidence.note: Independent ARC Prize evaluation (Dec 2024): o3 preview scored 75.7%/87.5% against GPT-4o's 5%, called a step-function increase. Caveats: training on ARC data and high compute.
METR preprint v1 (Mar 2025) finds the length of tasks AI can complete kept growing fast, possibly accelerating in 2024. It corroborates substantial gains.
The same evaluator notes o3 still fails easy tasks. That limits claims about AGI and reliability, not the size of the gain.

reviews.rationale: The forecast says every later improvement will be marginal. An independent December 2024 evaluation found a step-function gain, and METR's research independently corroborates fast progress. Together they meet the early-resolution rule. Caveats about benchmark-specific training and continuing failures do not make the gain marginal. The cost part is unresolved, but the claim is conjunctive, so it is contradicted.
